rounds.critic: Builder session 2 / trade, independent of infrastructure builder

models.observations: The doubled arcade, running water and ladder establish a credible public utility in all four ages. At 64 px the four little ends and few red keystones have very little presence. The Roman-style span dominates the faction markers.
defects: Enlarge a pair of opposed tusk corbels on a principal pier or end supports. Add clearly delineated sockets and keep the flowing channel clear. The pair should read at 64 px.

models.observations: The lifted trough and teal pipe stand apart against the light concrete. Ascension collars are distinct. Outside the large view the terminal teeth get lost against the narrow coping and the span reads as generic civil engineering.
defects: Enlarge a pair of opposed tusk corbels on a principal pier or end supports. Add clearly delineated sockets and keep the flowing channel clear. The pair should read at 64 px.

models.observations: Iron supply pipes and dark watercourse sit on red brick piers. The central ladder gives scale. In modern and industrial thumbnails the tiny teeth disappear into the parapet and nothing else carries a clear Orc profile.
defects: Enlarge a pair of opposed tusk corbels on a principal pier or end supports. Add clearly delineated sockets and keep the flowing channel clear. The pair should read at 64 px.

models.observations: The clamped teal core and a small horned service hall read as a reactor. The mounted fins hold the core visually. In the large image sections of the lower metal coil vanish where its facets dive into the core.
defects: Trace both metal coils on the reactor profile phase and scale the two axes to stand clear of the core over the whole band. The lower coil must remain continuous between fins.

models.observations: The two elevated wooden bins and sacks at the horned counting hut are readable in bronze and iron. Two levels of wooden binding break into alternating short dashes around both bins.
defects: Sweep both bin hoops using the same vertex phase and side count as the silo profile. Keep their inner clearance and outer face continuous round the slope at both edges of each hoop.

models.observations: Twin stone bins with hipped caps stand over a scale doorway and jars. In medieval the dashes on the dark bins look especially ragged where the binding intersects the wall.
defects: Sweep both bin hoops using the same vertex phase and side count as the silo profile. Keep their inner clearance and outer face continuous round the slope at both edges of each hoop.

models.observations: A top conveyor and three blue caps give the future grain stores their vertical rhythm. The bins have two lines of marks with fragments left on separated panels, stark on the bright information and ascension cladding.
defects: Sweep both bin hoops using the same vertex phase and side count as the silo profile. Keep their inner clearance and outer face continuous round the slope at both edges of each hoop.

models.observations: Three brick silos and their dark conveyor leave a clear packing yard for the sacks. The metal binding visibly breaks and reappears along both horizontal bands on the bins.
defects: Sweep both bin hoops using the same vertex phase and side count as the silo profile. Keep their inner clearance and outer face continuous round the slope at both edges of each hoop.

models.observations: The offset open cooling stacks and low roofed turbine hall form a distinct utility profile. Rim tusk and small horned cabinet echo the door horns. Pale concrete and blue roofs move to gold hardware in Ascension.
Stepped brick cooling stacks have dark open throats above their red collars. Domed hall with panel stripes and an entrance porch keeps the Orc industrial works distinct at 64 px.
Large freight door, beam scale, strapped bundle and broad hip roof identify a warehouse. The paired roof points and split door tusks frame the horizontal building through its three early rows.
The higher loading shed has a stone frame around its broad timber door, with a scale and strapped load at the side. Dark medieval materials preserve the silhouette of the ivory roof tips.
A crown skylight sits above the blue roof, a deep loading jamb and a covered scale. The broad door stays readable at the small size and the light crest tips remain distinguishable along the edges.
A projecting roof monitor lights a brick cargo shed. Dark steel bracing frames the side sling and strapped box. The small red wall banner and pale horns mark the front and roof.

Roofed lifting frame, visible water, wrapped rope drum and suspended bucket tell the function clearly. The light pitched hood and long horns crown the timber posts, and the second pail sits by the curb.

A masonry curb and narrow red band contrast with the water and suspended rope bucket. The taller roof leaves space to see the windlass and crank. The two horns and side bucket are visible in all three age skins.

The shallow glass hood, warm drum, metal crank and stepped stone ring distinguish this later well. The dark water and small hanging bucket remain visible under the arch. Gold metal reads on the Ascension variant.
An exposed flywheel and overhung beam replace the roof, keeping the hoist open to view. Brick curb, riveted drum and single horn contrast with the bright water and the little pail resting beside it.

rounds.critic: Builder session 2 / trade, independent of infrastructure builder

models.observations: Strong, paired tusk braces now rise above the central channel in all four ages. Their red sockets sit against the stone and the central access ladder remains clear.
An ivory crest now brackets the centre pier above the bright blue pipe and water line. Its tip remains visible at 64 px against both information and ascension masonry.
Bone corbels and seated red fittings mark the dark industrial channel from either side. The silhouette rises between the large spans, with clear water above the support.
The two clamping coils make continuous, well-defined bands between the reactor fins. They trace the cylinder across both the gold and blue variants. The small service hall anchors the scale.
Two clear courses follow the faceted sides of each early grain bin. The amber lids, horned packing hut and sacks frame the large and small vessels without visual interference.
Continuous bands wrap the paired masonry vessels through all three ages. They especially improve the dark medieval bindings against the pale silo walls.
Each pale silo now carries clearly formed circumferential metal bands. The gold version stays distinct in Ascension. Blue caps and the bridging conveyor remain readable above the hut.
Steel hoops sit continuously against the brick on each of the three bins, with clear separation between the two levels. The topped conveyor and low grain hut retain their contrasting scale.

At 64 px the broad hip roof reads as muted brown in Dawn, ochre bronze in Bronze and slate grey in Iron. The roof carries the age change across all three exported LODs. The wide cargo door and projecting hoist frame with its box stay legible at 120 triangles. The door tusks and red wall hanging are small at thumbnail size, while the roof tips retain their silhouette. The dominant-surface revision passes.
